newsitem.title: SWEDEN: P&U says negative trends to continue in 1997.
newsitem.headline: P&U says negative trends to continue in 1997.

text.p: Swedish-U.S. drug company Pharmacia & Upjohn said on Thursday negative sales and profit trends would continue this year but that it was taking measures to improve its results.

"Even though negative sales and profit trends will likely continue in 1997 and the result in the second quarter of 1997 may not be better than the first quarter's, we expected to take advantage of these measures in the beginning of 1998," it said.

Pharmacia & Upjohn said in a statement the company planned a series of measures to simplify P&U's structure and decision making systems, clarify division of responsibilities, and concentrate investments on research and developments.
The measures were only the first of several important decisions about strategy, operations and management, P&U said.
"Although they are initially concentrated on growth, we expect they will also give important cost savings which will be quantified later this year," P&U said.

Even though these initiatives would help turn around sales and worsening profits in the medium term and boost growth in the long term, P&U chief executive Fred Hassan said in the statement that significant advantages would not be apparent until 1998.
P&U posted a profit of 37 U.S. cents per share in the first quarter of the year.
P&U said it would phase out the group's three pharmaceutical product centres, in Stockholm, Milano, Italy and Kalamazoo, Michigan.
Sales, marketing and clinical tests in phase IV would be grouped in a division called Pharmaceutical Business which would be headed by a deputy CEO who would report to Hassan.
Further integration of research and development would come under Goran Ando.
A five-member committee would take on decision-making which was previously handled by a 19-member group, P&U said.
